title: Puppeteer service isolates renders and limits bodies without Content-Length
First-page reprint is limited to page 1
Mail and PDF renderers live in bundled-features, document-draft and signature print without injected functions
detail: The packages `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-mail-html` and `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-puppeteer-client` are removed. Their code ships as `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/renderer-mail-html` (plus `/renderer-mail-html/seeding`) and `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/renderer-puppeteer-client` (plus `/renderer-puppeteer-client/qualified-names`) with the same exports, feature names, entity `rendered-pdf`, table and environment variables, so no data migration is needed. `createDocumentDraftFeature` loses its `pdf` option and its type parameter, `createSignatureFeature` loses `renderHtmlToPdf`; both render through the print client themselves and require the `renderer-puppeteer-client` feature at boot. The types `DocumentDraftPdf` and `RenderSignatureHtmlToPdf` are gone.
migration: Replace the two package names in imports and package.json with the `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/renderer-mail-html` and `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/renderer-puppeteer-client` subpaths (keep one bundled-features dependency). Then delete the `pdf: { render, store }` option from `createDocumentDraftFeature(...)` and `renderHtmlToPdf` from `createSignatureFeature(...)`, and mount `createRendererPuppeteerClientFeature()` wherever document-draft or signature is mounted.

image-snapshot HTML must embed every resource as a data URI
detail: An earlier release note said image-snapshot requests were unchanged. Since the puppeteer-service egress guard, the service fetches no http(s) resources for any request kind, so external img, link and font references in an image-snapshot are dropped without an error.
migration: Embed images, fonts and stylesheets in image-snapshot HTML as data: URIs before sending payload.content.

title: image-snapshot width and height come from the image header; PDF default layout slug is shared
Render requests retry only network errors, 502 and 503, and the timeout covers the body
renderAndStorePdf is removed; render in beforeTransaction with renderPdfBeforeTransaction and store with storeRenderedPdf
detail: renderAndStorePdf called the print service inside the write transaction and held a pool connection for the whole render. renderPdfBeforeTransaction(ctx, { slug, locale, variables, attachTo? }) now renders and uploads the PDF before the transaction opens, and storeRenderedPdf(ctx, event.prepared) writes the fileRef and rendered-pdf rows inside it. RenderAndStorePdfArgs is renamed RenderPdfArgs.
migration: Move the render into the handler's beforeTransaction phase and store in the handler: defineWriteHandler({ name, schema, access, beforeTransaction: (event, ctx) => renderPdfBeforeTransaction(ctx, { slug: "invoice", locale: "de", variables }), handler: (event, ctx) => storeRenderedPdf(ctx, event.prepared) }). The result of storeRenderedPdf has the same shape as the old renderAndStorePdf result (StoredRenderedPdf). Rename the RenderAndStorePdfArgs type to RenderPdfArgs. A handler with a beforeTransaction phase cannot be called through a nested ctx.write; call it as a top-level command.

title: renders document-pdf from templates, adds renderAndStorePdf, the rendered-pdf entity and puppeteer-status
detail: The plugin resolves the document-pdf template and its pdf-layout (header, signature, footer), embeds every image as a data URI and sends finished HTML to the puppeteer-service. renderAndStorePdf(ctx, { slug, locale, variables, attachTo? }) stores the PDF as a file and a rendered-pdf record with the template and layout version. The puppeteer-status query reports whether the service answers; while it does not, rendering fails with PuppeteerUnavailableError (HTTP 503, puppeteer_unavailable). The feature adds the table rendered_pdfs.
migration: Call renderAndStorePdf(ctx, { slug, locale, variables, attachTo? }) from a write handler; no escape hatch or rendererDb is needed because the tenant db also reads system templates and files. Apps that mount renderer-puppeteer-client need a schema migration for rendered_pdfs (`kumiko schema generate`). PUPPETEER_SERVICE_URL and PUPPETEER_AUTH_TOKEN stay as before. image-snapshot requests are unchanged.

title: The service performs no network fetches
Query preview-pdf prints a document draft to a real PDF
Package moved to the framework under the @cosmicdrift scope
detail: Renamed from @cosmicdriftgamestudio/kumiko-renderer-puppeteer-client (GitHub Packages, kumiko-enterprise) to @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-puppeteer-client on npmjs. The rename itself changes no API; the other 0.363.0 entries list the API changes of this release.
migration: Replace @cosmicdriftgamestudio/kumiko-renderer-puppeteer-client with @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-puppeteer-client in package.json and in every import; install from npmjs instead of GitHub Packages.
